paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: love in this song doesn't sit still. He comes leaping, and he calls, "Arise, my darling." (Song of Solomon 2:10) And when she can't find him, she doesn't roll over and hit snooze. She says, "I will arise now and go about the city…" (Song of Solomon 3:2)

Then there are the little foxes. The song talks about "the little foxes that ruin the vineyards" and says the vineyards are in bloom (Song of Solomon 2:15). I think that tells us something in bloom is worth guarding, and it's the small stuff that sneaks in. She sums up what she has with "My beloved is mine and I am his" (Song of Solomon 2:16), and that kind of belonging is worth the watching.

She finishes with a charge to the daughters of Jerusalem: "Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right." (Song of Solomon 3:5) Love is a good thing, so it deserves good timing. Pull a batch out early and you're not holding cookies, you're holding warm, sad dough. So take it seriously, baker, and let it come in its time.
